gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI's US store sells the AC180 and the Elite 100 V2 for the same $499 today (2026-11-15), and that OutdoorGearLab measured 950 Wh usable from the AC180 against 890 Wh from the Elite 100 V2. So at the same price, the older model gives about 7% more measured energy ($0.53 vs $0.56 per measured Wh) and weighs 11 lb more.
standout_why: I compared five pages. The cited OutdoorGearLab AC180 review gives the 950 Wh figure but no current price, and it only says the Elite 100 V2 has a 'lower street price'. preparedstates.com (result 14, updated 2026-11-14) lists both at $499 with weights, but no measured usable Wh and no cost per Wh. offgridbenchmark has not tested the AC180: it lists it at $699 and estimates about 980 Wh. ChatGPT's own answer calls the AC180 a 'discounted older-model option' with no price and picks the Elite 100 V2 as 'best value' at $499. I could not open the cited Yahoo/CNET page (HTTP 403). No page I read puts measured Wh next to today's price for these two models.
decides: The finding backs the Elite 100 V2 as the overall pick for anything you carry: it is 25 lb vs 36 lb, OutdoorGearLab calls it quieter, and it costs the same. It also changes how the AC180 should be framed. It is not 'only at a deep discount'. At $499 (store compare-at price $1,232) it gives the most measured energy for $499 in BLUETTI's range, for a buyer who keeps the unit at home. One step up, the Elite 200 V2 at $899 costs $0.43 per rated Wh, less than the Elite 100 V2's $0.49. The Elite 300 at $1,199 has the lowest cost per rated Wh in the range at $0.40.
